description:
Follow-ups from a deep post-merge review of the shipped DuckLake adapter
(#1082 core adapter, #1096 catalog backends + S3; both in _project/DONE/).
The confirmed credential leak is tracked separately and gates this item
(see deps.needs: ducklake-postgres-credential-leak-redaction).

Headline risk is COVERAGE, not code: the adapter's core live behavior runs in
ZERO CI lanes. tests/integration/test_ducklake_integration.py is module-marked
`slow`; the core in-process ATTACH class (TestDuckLakeLiveConnection) and the
Postgres/S3 classes additionally carry `live_integration`. Every default lane
selects `not (slow or ... or live_integration)`; the `-m slow` PR jobs are
file-scoped to OTHER files; release-canary/validate-main-pr exclude
live_integration. Net: classes 1/3/4 run in no lane; the SQLite class runs only
at the main-release gate -- never on the develop PR that merged it. Both feature
PRs squash-auto-merged with no human review (platforms/ is not a CODEOWNERS
path). The Postgres and S3 classes have never executed anywhere.

Two related process blind spots are recorded under _project/blind-spots/
(auto-revert blame heuristic; slow+live_integration coverage theater).

deferrals.reason: Requires new phase instrumentation; the coarse ducklake-vs-duckdb comparison is available today. Track only if w11/w12 conclude attribution is required for beta.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] duplicate: Sub-task of the still-open parent item; belongs inside its existing work items rather than a new TODO. (tracked by ducklake-post-merge-review-followups)
deferrals.summary: Fine-grained attribution of catalog-metadata ops vs Parquet-scan vs engine time

deferrals.reason: making deployment_mode functional is new behaviour, outside w10's modelling fix
deferrals.summary: DuckLake deployment_modes are inert: adapter_factory resolves --platform ducklake:<mode> and passes config['deployment_mode'], but benchbox/platforms/ducklake.py never reads it. So 'ducklake:postgres_catalog_s3' silently runs a local duckdb-file catalog on local disk. w10 fixed the MODELLING (four modes on the real axes) and the descriptions now say selection is via --platform-option catalog= + the data_path scheme, but a user can still select a mode that does nothing. Either map modes to option defaults (explicit options winning) or reject a mode that contradicts the resolved axes

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/platform_registry.py:128 ducklake deployment_modes (two orthogonal axes encoded as three pseudo-modes) — SUPERSEDE/annotate (w10)
benchbox/platforms/ducklake.py:527-544 handle_existing_database local metadata_path reuse detection — SUPERSEDE for postgres with a server-side probe (w6)
tests/integration/platforms/test_postgresql_live.py skip_unless_docker_service + the nightly live_postgresql job — REUSE the docker-service bring-up pattern for the PG class (w1)
tests/unit/test_marker_strategy.py + `make lint-markers` (CI-only marker gate) — EXTEND with a lane-coverage meta-check (w4)

verifications.description: PG and S3 live classes execute (not skip) against real infra and pass
verifications.expected: PG + S3 classes run and pass (or reveal fixable failures), not silently skipped

verifications.description: Lane-coverage meta-check flags any zero-lane integration module
verifications.expected: test_ducklake_integration.py is selected by at least one lane after w3

work_units.evidence: Brought up PostgreSQL 18 via Apple Containerization (mocker run postgres:18; note -p forwarding does NOT work - reach it at the container IP, PG_DUCKLAKE_HOST=192.168.64.2). TestDuckLakePostgresCatalogLive PASSES. Verified w6 end-to-end: run1 reused=False, run2 no-force reused=True (was the crash), run3 force -> 0 tables left. ducklake_table rows are tombstoned via end_snapshot, not stranded. FOUND+FIXED a real defect: --force left local Parquet on disk for postgres catalogs (1 -> 0 files after fix)
work_units.notes:
Find the make docker-postgres target (e.g. make test-docker-up-postgresql).
Pre-create the ducklake_catalog database (adapter does NOT CREATE DATABASE).
Run: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration/test_ducklake_integration.py -m live_integration -n 0 -k Postgres
Report and fix every failure. This class has never executed against a real server.
work_units.summary: Bring up live PostgreSQL, pre-create the catalog DB, and run the DuckLake PG live_integration class; fix what breaks

work_units.evidence: platform_registry.py ducklake deployment_modes: 3 pseudo-modes -> 4 on the real axes (catalog backend x storage location). The old model had cloud_storage carrying mode=local and made postgres-catalog+S3 unrepresentable; new modes local, local_catalog_s3, postgres_catalog, postgres_catalog_s3 with accurate creds/cloud/network flags. notes rewritten to state the two axes; landing catalog.generated.js regenerated. 8246 tests pass
work_units.notes:
platform_registry.py:128 encodes catalog(duckdb/sqlite/postgres) x storage(local/s3)
as local/postgres_catalog/cloud_storage. Consequence: `ducklake:postgres_catalog`
validates (adapter_factory.py:190) but does nothing (adapter reads only
catalog=), and docs/platforms/comparison-matrix.md:81 lists them beside real
:mode platforms as mutually exclusive. Collapse to one mode or mark the entries
descriptive-only; correct the matrix row.
work_units.summary: Fix the deployment_modes modeling: two orthogonal axes (catalog backend x storage location) presented as three exclusive pseudo-modes

work_units.evidence: docs/development/adr/adr-ducklake-maturity-and-publishability.md decision w11: 5 concrete criteria; 1/2/4 met (PR-lane coverage #1357, live PG+S3 2026-07-30, server-side reuse/force verified), criterion 3 (TPC-H SF>=1 on all four deployment modes through the correctness gate) NOT met and is now the single blocker - ducklake stays experimental
work_units.notes: None exists (registry only records support_status: experimental). Write measurable criteria.
work_units.summary: Define the concrete experimental -> beta exit criterion for the ducklake platform

work_units.evidence: ADR decision w12: remote-backed runs ARE publishable and ranking-eligible under existing trust labels, but must record catalog backend + storage location; grounded in provenance.py mapping source (not infrastructure) to trust label. Reframed the risk as comparison-grouping, not publication. Revisit when w11 criterion 3 scale runs exist
work_units.notes:
Network variance sits inside every timed phase (per-query S3 GET in
execute_query; PG catalog round-trips in ATTACH/commit). No annotation flags
remote-backed runs. Decide: quarantine/annotate vs allow to published-results.
work_units.summary: Decide the publishability policy for remote-backed (PG catalog / S3 storage) DuckLake results

work_units.evidence: ADR decision w13: NO. Decided on evidence that code-owner approval enforcement was RETIRED 2026-07-18 (repo-admin-settings.md) - CODEOWNERS now only mirrors SOUNDNESS_PREFIXES for auto-merge withholding + routes review. Adding benchbox/platforms/** would withhold auto-merge on the highest-churn tree for zero review benefit; adapters produce numbers, the owner-reviewed correctness gate adjudicates them
work_units.notes:
#1082/#1096 merged via squash auto-merge, no human review; platforms/ is not a
soundness path. Decide whether to add benchbox/platforms/** (or new adapters)
to .github/CODEOWNERS + auto_merge_soundness_paths.py.
work_units.summary: Decide whether platform adapters that produce publishable numbers should be a CODEOWNERS owner-review path

work_units.evidence: ADR decision w14 + docs/platforms/ducklake.md caveat: DOCUMENT, not instrument. Verified BenchBox never invokes compaction/inlining and measured 5 INSERTs -> 5 parquet files. Bias direction stated: runs AGAINST DuckLake (numbers are a floor), so readers can reason about the gap; instrumenting would change what is measured or add result-schema surface
work_units.notes:
The adapter runs no compaction/merge/inlining between load and query; a
multi-batch load leaves many small Parquet files. If a competitor auto-compacts
and DuckLake doesn't, scan-time comparisons are unfair. Settle with a
load->compact->query vs load->query timing delta, then instrument or annotate.
work_units.summary: Decide whether absence of DuckLake compaction/inlining biases cross-engine comparisons; instrument or document

work_units.evidence: TestDuckLakeS3DataPathLive PASSES against real S3 (existing benchbox-athena bucket, unique benchbox_ducklake_test/<run_id> prefix, credential_chain provider; AWS creds passed by inline shell substitution, never written to a file). Nothing to fix - the class works as written. Also confirmed w7's premise empirically: after the test DROPped its table, the Parquet object remained in the bucket (1 object, 472B) - real orphaned storage. Test prefix deleted afterwards; bucket left as found
work_units.notes:
Set BENCHBOX_S3_TEST_BUCKET + AWS creds and run the S3 class
(-m live_integration -k S3). Never executed. Exercise both credential_chain
and explicit KEY_ID/SECRET paths, and force-recreate leaving orphaned Parquet (see w7).
work_units.summary: Run the DuckLake S3 data_path live_integration class against a real bucket; fix what breaks

work_units.evidence: Dropped live_integration from TestDuckLakeLiveConnection (needs no external service, unlike the Postgres/S3 classes which keep it) + new pr.yml step running the module with -m 'slow and not live_integration'. Measured: non-fast lane collection 1/9 -> 7/9; the exact CI step passes locally 7 passed 2 deselected in 31s
work_units.notes:
TestDuckLakeLiveConnection needs only the ducklake extension (no external
service) yet is live_integration -> runs nowhere. Re-marker it (or add a
lane) so core ATTACH/cursor-scoping/force-recreate/platform_info is exercised
on develop PRs. Keep PG/S3 classes live_integration.
work_units.summary: Give the extension-only in-process ATTACH class a marker a real lane runs, so core adapter behavior is gated in CI

work_units.evidence: tests/unit/test_marker_strategy.py: two meta-checks - test_every_integration_module_is_selected_by_at_least_one_lane (per-module, evaluates the 7 tree-wide lane expressions via a marker-namespace eval, exempts module-level opt-in and workflow-named paths) and test_opt_in_markers_below_module_level_are_declared_service_dependent (per-class, the one with real power). First design was per-module only and FAILED its own mutation test - restoring live_integration on the service-free class still passed because a sibling covered test hid it; the per-class check now fails naming the class. 10 passed, make lint-markers green, 4 genuinely service-dependent classes allowlisted with reasons
work_units.notes:
Resolve each test module's module+class markers against every workflow/Makefile
`-m` expression; fail if any module matches no lane. Prevents future
coverage-theater. Model on test_marker_strategy.py / lint-markers.
work_units.summary: Add a CI meta-check that fails when an integration test module is selected by zero configured lanes

work_units.evidence: tests/integration/test_ducklake_integration.py: _probe_extension records the failure reason in _PROBE_FAILURES and warnings.warn()s once (cache makes one failure decide the session); _skip_unless_extensions now cites the recorded reason in every skip message it causes
work_units.notes:
tests/integration/test_ducklake_integration.py: DUCKLAKE_AVAILABLE =
@cache _probe_extension('ducklake') runs at import/collection; a transient
extension-repo blip caches False and silently skips even the SQLite class that
gates release-canary. Emit a warning/xfail (not a silent skip) at the release gate.
work_units.summary: Make _probe_extension's cached-False outcome loud instead of a silent session-wide skip

work_units.evidence: benchbox/platforms/ducklake.py: _resolve_postgres_catalog_reuse() + _existing_lake_tables() resolve reuse/force post-ATTACH for catalog=postgres (the pre-connection hook cannot - no local metadata file); force drops the catalog's tables server-side, no-force sets database_was_reused=True so the runner skips the CREATE TABLE that crashed reruns
work_units.notes:
handle_existing_database keys off local metadata_path.exists(), never true for
a server-side PG catalog -> database_was_reused stays False -> second run hits
inherited plain CREATE TABLE -> 'table already exists' crash; --force is a no-op.
Probe the PG catalog server-side (ducklake metadata tables) for reuse; honor
--force by dropping/recreating the catalog schema. NOTE: current behavior
crashes (safe) rather than silently misreporting cold-load timings -- confirmed.
work_units.summary: Postgres catalog reuse/force: server-side detection so reruns don't crash and --force works

work_units.evidence: benchbox/platforms/ducklake.py _reset_ducklake_catalog(): cloud DATA_PATH now emits an explicit logger.warning naming the prefix + the aws s3 rm remedy instead of silently leaving orphaned Parquet; docs/platforms/ducklake.md gains a what---force-clears table and a warning admonition. Chose the 'document' arm over 'clear the prefix': recursive object-store deletion is destructive, the prefix may hold data this run did not write, and results stay correct (the rebuilt catalog references only new files) - the harm is storage cost, not correctness
work_units.notes:
_reset_ducklake_catalog correctly guards rmtree with `not _data_path_is_cloud`
(no dangerous deletion -- verified), but cloud data is never reset; new catalog
only references new files (results stay correct) yet storage leaks. Clear the
prefix via the cloud client on force, or document the leak.
work_units.summary: --force with cloud (s3) DATA_PATH leaves orphaned Parquet; clear the prefix or document

work_units.evidence: pyproject.toml: new 'ducklake' extra pinning duckdb>=1.3.0,<2.0.0 (the duckdb extra stays >=1.0 for results.duckdb on-disk-format compat); registry installation_command now 'uv add benchbox[ducklake]' instead of the floorless 'uv add duckdb'
work_units.notes:
pyproject pins duckdb>=1.0.0,<2.0.0; uv sync can resolve 1.2 which cannot load
ducklake. Mitigated by a clean runtime guard (ducklake.py:606) so it's not a
confusing failure -- but an optional-dependency extra `ducklake=["duckdb>=1.3,<2.0"]`
or a documented requirement would prevent a broken environment.
work_units.summary: Express the duckdb>=1.3 floor installably (ducklake extra) or document the requirement

work_units.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] DuckLake bullet now states the shipped feature: catalog backend x data_path axes (incl. postgres catalog + S3), reuse/--force, and the benchbox[ducklake] extra - was describing only the #1082 MVP (DuckDB-file catalog + local Parquet). Edit is in [Unreleased], not a retrospective edit to a shipped section
work_units.notes:
#1096's scope_limit forbade the CHANGELOG edit and no follow-up corrected it;
the unreleased notes still say 'DuckDB-file catalog + local Parquet storage'.
work_units.summary: Correct CHANGELOG.md to reflect the shipped feature (sqlite/postgres catalogs + S3), not just the #1082 MVP
